precepts.text: Who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? The wise man. The thing that have been is talking about man. Man has been around before, but there's no remembrance of us being around before.
precepts.point: The thing that hath been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun. Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? It hath been already of old time, which was before us: before our generation, it was in the past. And there is no remembrance of former things.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing. And “a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine”.

The thing that hath been, in Ecclesiastes 1, is talking about man. Man has been around before, but “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” It takes wisdom to interpret that thing.

So the wise man understands the cycle: the generations pass and come again, and what the prophets already saw is what we are living out now. The wise man knows it is man that hath been, and that is why there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction. Yes, we sinned against our God, and the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies, but they took it too far.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

The Lord says it in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” Yes, we sinned against our God. Yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies. But they took it too far.

God was but a little displeased with Israel, and the heathen helped forward the affliction. You think Christ ain't see that? That is why Esau's rule over Jacob is to his own hurt: he went past what God allowed, and the Lord is sore displeased with him for it.

precepts.text: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. Through all our slavery the Lord saw all of it, and when he comes back he is going to repay all of that pain and suffering. Salvation is not for the oppressors; salvation is for those who have been afflicted.

precepts.why:
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them”. In all of our affliction, through all of our slavery, the Lord saw all of it.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

The Lord has not forgotten. They will be taken in the snare. It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.text: The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate. That is twofold: it is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Sirach said vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for the proud. Jeremiah shows the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

The destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, to make the land desolate, without an inhabitant.

And that is twofold. It is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ. The lion that came up against the land in the days of Jeremiah is a picture of the Lion that is coming for the nations that ruled over Israel to their own hurt.

precepts.text: Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly. Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel, and he dealt unjustly in it. They shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people; the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us, like we read in Ephesians 2. O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us: the Babylonians, the Assyrians, and every ruler since. They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness”. If favour was shown to Esau, he still wouldn't change his wicked ways. It does not pay to be wicked.

“in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel. And what did he do there? He stole it. He will not behold the majesty of the Lord: he changes his image to a white man with stringy blonde hair and blue eyes.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people”. The people are God's chosen people, the ones the heathen envy in 2 Esdras 2:28. “yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”, like we read earlier in Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies.

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us”: like the so-called white man, like the Babylonians, like the Assyrians. “but by thee only will we make mention of thy name. They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” All of our enemies, all of these other lords that had rule over us, are dead. That is the hurt of the man that ruled over another.

precepts.text: The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord. They cannot stop it, because they are not going to be in rulership any more.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Isaiah said the wicked shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people. Who are those people? God's chosen people. Ezra says it: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.”

The heathen shall envy the Israelites. But they shall be able to do nothing. They can't stop it, because they ain't going to be in rulership any more. They are not going to have ownership any more.

That is the end of the man who ruleth over another to his own hurt: the time of his rule runs out, and all his envy cannot stop what the Lord has spoken for Israel.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
precepts.point: Having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience when your obedience is fulfilled. Brothers want to be on the Saturday night specials casting out demons in the street, but you cannot revenge disobedience until there is no impediment to sin left in your own spirit, your household, and your children.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
The weapons of our warfare are the commandments. You are supposed to answer your impulses, your sinful temptations, with the commandments of God, and that is supposed to turn you from the door of temptation. If you understood that death is around the corner, you would listen to these laws.

But the wicked man thinks judgment is far off: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Because the judgment is not immediate, his sick, evil mind is emboldened to commit evil and sin, and he leaves the commandments to the side. You had better recognize where you are.

That is the war inside you. The Lord isn't asking you to pick up a gun and go do something out there; he is asking you to get your mind right and set this mark in your head to change your behavior. We don't advocate anyone initiating aggression; if someone comes at you with a rope or a knife, you defend yourself. But the gung-ho brothers who can't wait for war can't even discipline their food. The war to win first is against the heart that sin makes bold.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, men's hearts are set to do evil.
precepts.point: They married the nations' daughters, and the holy seed was mingled.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites “have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations”. They married the nations' daughters, and the holy seed was mixed. It is like that today: the pollution of the Gentiles is evil-ass Christmas. And it is the brothers with an affinity for the white woman, the Japanese, the Moabitess, the Arab; the brothers secretly dealing with prostitutes and escorts; the brothers wasting the holy seed that could have been a prophet, an avenger, your son, and shooting him in a sock and down the drain. You either kill the old man within you, or you are going to catch an STD and be killed. That is the judgment of the Lord.

Why do men keep rolling the dice? Solomon says it: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” The judgment of the Lord for the evil you do in the dark, outside of this congregation, is not executed immediately on brothers and sisters, so the heart, which is the mind, is fully set to keep doing it over and over again.

But things lie dormant. The Lord may let it manifest, bubble and marinate in you, and then say: this brother or sister gives not a damn about my laws; I showed him mercy and longsuffering; now I have to execute him. A slow death: AIDS, HIV, gonorrhea, syphilis. The Lord says, I'm going to get you one way or the next; I gave you a chance to repent, but you are hardheaded. And a hard head makes a soft ass. Then you are crying out to God, and he is not hearing you.

So the delay of the sentence is not permission; it is time to repent. Kill that old man before you are killed.

precepts.text: A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed; that is why Moses' face shone.
precepts.point: Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.”

That is why the skin of Moses' face shone when he came down from mount Sinai, and he wist it not. This was no ordinary wisdom Moses was getting; he was getting the utmost wisdom, and it made his face shine so that Aaron and all the children of Israel were afraid to come nigh him.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of men is fully set in them to do evil, which is why Amon's evil increased.
precepts.point: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.”

That is why Amon’s evil increased. He saw his father’s idols stand and took up serving them, and with no sentence executed speedily his heart was fully set to do evil: he “humbled not himself before the Lord”, “but Amon trespassed more and more.” He reigned only “two years in Jerusalem” before “his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.”

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil.
precepts.point: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” That answers Job's question: “Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?” Because the sentence is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil. They live and grow old in it because the judgment has not yet fallen. This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.

precepts.text: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times and his days be prolonged, yet it shall be well with them that fear God.
precepts.point: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? This verse opens the whole thread on how the wicked do prosper.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why: “Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him”. The wicked do live, become old, and are mighty in power; a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged. But that is not the end of it: yet it shall be well with them that fear God. The prolonged days of the wicked are no proof that they are right; it is well with them that fear before him.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the hearts of men are set to do evil; grace differs for each person.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
God is angry with the wicked every day, but he does not strike every day. “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.”

Because the sentence does not come right away, the hearts of men are set to do evil. They mistake the mercy for approval. The grace differs for each person; that space to repent is not the same for everyone, so do not take the delay as a sign that God is not angry.

That mercy is Christ. Every day we wake up, thank God for his son, because it is his mercy holding back the fury and giving even those who disrespect Christ a chance to repent before the sentence is executed.

precepts.text: A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, the wisdom of knowing the interpretation of a thing.
precepts.point: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, so the Israelites are to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness. Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not Thy law.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; and teach me thy statutes.” “Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.”

A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, the wisdom of knowing the interpretation of a thing. When the Most High teaches his servant his statutes, that wisdom is what makes the face shine.

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, we get comfortable sinning and set our hearts fully to do evil once we get away with it.
precepts.point: Though Israel clothes herself with crimson and gold and paints her face, in vain does she make herself fair, for her lovers, the nations she followed, will despise her and seek her life; the voice of the daughter of Zion is heard mourning.

note.label: Jeremiah 4: Return unto Me, or Destruction from the North

precepts.why:
Israel clothes herself with crimson and gold and paints her face, making herself fair in vain, right up until the whole city flees at the noise of the horsemen and bowmen. Solomon explains how a people gets that comfortable in sin: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.”

Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, we get comfortable sinning and set our hearts fully to do evil once we get away with it. Then the lovers, the nations she followed, despise her and seek her life, and the voice of the daughter of Zion is heard mourning, Woe is me now.
